newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest blue chips take bourse volumes higher.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest blue chips take bourse volumes higher.

text.p: Bucharest bourse volumes and turnover picked up on Tuesday on the back of stronger interest in several blue chips, especially Oltchim.
But average prices of more than half the 54 stocks slipped in what dealers called "lazy summer trading."
"Overall trading was light, with the second tier dormant, but Oltchim and pharmaceuticals boosted turnover in the top section," said a trader.

Three independent indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, inched higher by 1.8, 1.75 and 1.77 percent respectively from Monday to 1,366.7, 1,463.1 and 1,873 points.
Volume increased to 2.5 million shares from 1.7 million and turnover added 3.5 billion lei to 10.7 billion.
The first tier took 76 percent of total volume and 89 percent of turnover. Oltchim traded most actively, with 740,400 shares changing hands on turnover of 3.3 billion lei.

Traders said strong demand throughout the session had helped Oltchim gain eight percent on its average price and had also led it to a 350 lei firmer close of 4,500. They said market news on its pending privatisation was behind the rise.
Antibiotice and Terapia pharmaceuticals were also active, with a total 2.8 billion lei in turnover. Terapia climbed 100 lei to end at 11,300 and Antibiotice closed flat at 7,950.
Brokers said there had been interest also in refrigerator maker Arctic, which traded over 270,000 shares. It weakened 100 lei to 3,300, as pressure eased in late trading.
On the second tier, Ciprom oil drilling equipment maker traded more actively, as some 200,000 shares changed hands. It ended 20 lei stronger at 1,030.
Brokers welcomed the news of an official bourse index to be launched next month. "It will be a barometer, confirming the market has grown more liquid and also stronger," said one.
